test_title: PYST 5: SSC Stenographer - English (Held On:18 Nov 2022 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.**

“Leave me alone” yelled the little boy in the movie, “or else I will start shouting loudly.”

options.text: The little boy in the movie shouted that he should be left alone or else he would start shouting loudly.
The little boy wanted to be left alone or else he will start shouting loudly.
The little boy in the movie cried to be left alone or else he shall start shouting loudly.
The little boy requested to be left alone or else he would start shouting loudly.

solution:
The correct answer is **The little boy in the movie shouted that he should be left alone or else he would start shouting loudly.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When transforming the original sentence to indirect speech, the structure and the tense primarily needs to be changed.
 
• For transforming the verbs tense: "will start" becomes "would start".
 
• This is known as "backshift". In this case, "will" (future simple tense) turns into "would" (conditional).
 
• The word "yelled" provides an assertion of the boy raising his voice, which is why the term "shouted" should be used in reported speech. 
 
• "Leave me alone" is an imperative sentence in direct speech. It's a command or a plea from the speaker, the little boy.
 
• In indirect speech, to maintain the same meaning but to eliminate the direct command, we use a different structure using : subject + should + base verb.
 
• Here, "me" which is the first person singular pronoun in the direct speech is changed to "he", the third person singular pronoun in the indirect speech.
 
• This is because the subject of the direct speech is the little boy who said "Leave me alone", and in reported speech we refer to this same person in third person as "he".
 
• The imperative verb "Leave" changes to "should be left".
 
• Here, the modal verb "should" is added to emphasize the obligation or directive nature of the command, but in a more polite, less direct form.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**
